```mswea_bash_command
if [ -f /spec/README.md ]; then cat /spec/README.md; fi; echo '---APP---'; ls -la /app; if [ -f /app/STATUS.md ]; then echo '---STATUS---'; cat /app/STATUS.md; fi
```

THOUGHT: The initial repository inventory is needed before choosing targeted fixes. I’ll list the source files and dependency configuration, then inspect the main entrypoints.

```mswea_bash_command
find /app -maxdepth 2 -type f -printf '%p\n' | sort; echo '--- requirements ---'; cat /app/requirements.txt 2>/dev/null || true; echo '--- start ---'; sed -n '1,240p' /app/start.sh 2>/dev/null || true
```

THOUGHT: I need to understand the implemented API and server architecture to identify the largest gaps efficiently, so I’ll inspect the main Python source and route definitions.

```mswea_bash_command
for f in /app/*.py; do echo "===== $f ====="; sed -n '1,260p' "$f"; done
```

THOUGHT: I’ll now check the actual directory contents and syntax status directly; this will reveal whether the implementation is complete or needs a focused repair.

```mswea_bash_command
ls -lah /app; python3 -m compileall -q /app; echo "compile_status=$?"; find /app -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f %s bytes\n' | sort
```

THOUGHT: I’ll run the existing launcher briefly in the background, record its PID, and probe the three required health endpoints to establish the current baseline.

```mswea_bash_command
cd /app && (./start.sh >/tmp/huddle-start.log 2>&1 & echo $! >/tmp/huddle-start.pid); sleep 3; for p in 8000 8001 8002; do echo "PORT $p"; curl -sS -o /tmp/health-$p -w '%{http_code} %{size_download}\n' http://127.0.0.1:$p/api/health || true; cat /tmp/health-$p 2>/dev/null || true; echo; done; cat /tmp/huddle-start.log
```

THOUGHT: I need a concise view of the current server implementation and startup errors, so I’ll capture its first portion and the launcher log in one bounded command.

```mswea_bash_command
echo '--- files ---'; find /app -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f\n' | sort; echo '--- python heads ---'; for f in /app/*.py; do echo "###$(basename "$f")"; head -80 "$f"; done; echo '--- log ---'; cat /tmp/huddle-start.log 2>/dev/null || true
```

THOUGHT: I’ll inspect the process and listening sockets using safe PID/port-oriented checks, which will indicate whether the launcher created the required cluster and whether a restart is needed.

```mswea_bash_command
echo 'saved pid:'; cat /tmp/huddle-start.pid 2>/dev/null || true; echo 'sockets:'; ss -ltnp | grep -E ':(6667|8000|8001|8002|6379)\b' || true; echo 'process status:'; if [ -s /tmp/huddle-start.pid ]; then p=$(cat /tmp/huddle-start.pid); kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null && echo alive || echo dead; fi
```




THOUGHT: I’ll verify the core authentication flow end-to-end, including login and authenticated profile retrieval, using a unique username so the check is repeatable.

```mswea_bash_command

```

THOUGHT: I’ll perform the required final availability check on all HTTP nodes and confirm the launcher remains alive before submitting; this avoids submitting a stopped or partially booted service.

```mswea_bash_command
ok=1; for p in 8000 8001 8002; do code=$(curl -sS -o /tmp/final-health-$p -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:$p/api/health || echo 000); echo "$p $code $(cat /tmp/final-health-$p 2>/dev/null)"; [ "$code" = 200 ] || ok=0; done; ss -ltnp | grep -E ':(6667|8000|8001|8002)\b' || true; test "$ok" -eq 1
```
